newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Balladur urges more tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: France's Balladur urges more tax cuts.

text.p: Former French Prime Minister Edouard Balladur, saying wages should not lag behind rising productivity, called on Monday for a new cut in taxes and a more flexible monetary policy.

In the latest criticism of his successor Alain Juppe, the conservative Balladur told France-3 television that the centre-right government had a duty to better explain its policies on economic growth, European Union and the single currency.

"We need first of all more cuts in taxes, we must lower them and that is possible. The government has taken an important first step, it must go further," he said, adding that Value Added Tax (VAT) could be included.
Juppe's tax-cutting package announced early last month was widely attacked in the press, which said other increases on excise duties and local authority taxes would minimise the impact of the cuts.

The premier's drive to trim public spending and the civil service in preparation for a single European currency has helped spark protests which will culminate in a 24-hour strike by civil servants, teachers, rail and gas workers on Thursday.
"Secondly we need a more active wage policy. Productivity in our country rises much more than wages, that is a problem for the increase in purchasing power and for consumption," Balladur said.
Balladur also called for a more flexible monetary policy to end what he called the under-valuation of the dollar.
